core-policy.observation: Pepr mutates/validates non-root execution, no privilege escalation and dropped capabilities, including init and ephemeral containers; exemptions are explicit.

core-network.observation: Operator generates namespace ingress/egress default-deny NetworkPolicy; connectivity requires declared allow rules.

core-mtls.observation: Root-namespace PeerAuthentication requires STRICT mTLS. Horizon opts into ambient mesh; in-mesh plaintext-looking URLs are protected by mesh rather than application TLS.

core-gateway.observation: Gateway redirects HTTP to HTTPS and requires TLS 1.3 by default, optionally TLS 1.2; credentialName references Kubernetes TLS secrets.

core-accesslog.observation: Istio access logs go to stdout; path normalization merges slashes, proxies are held until ready, and forwarded certificate details are sanitized.

core-vector.observation: Vector Agent collects Kubernetes pod and node log files, labels namespace/container/host, uses acknowledged disk buffers, and ships continuously to Loki; metrics are exported.

core-loki.observation: Loki uses ambient mesh; ingress is limited to Grafana, Vector, FalcoSidekick and monitoring service identities; object-store egress is declared separately.

core-grafana.observation: Grafana disables local login, uses UDS OAuth, maps Admin group to Admin and Auditor to Viewer, and rejects unmatched groups. OAuth secrets are file-mounted.

core-retention.observation: Loki default retains logs indefinitely; configured compactor retention and external bucket lifecycle can change this. Retention capacity and required archive policy remain deployment responsibilities.

core-velero.observation: Velero schedules daily backups at 03:00 with 240-hour TTL, but snapshotVolumes=false and snapshotsEnabled=false; default resource backups do not establish PostgreSQL PVC data recovery.

core-falco.observation: Falco loads shipped rule sets, detects runtime behavior and ships Sidekick events to Loki. Alertmanager delivery is commented out; detection is not automatic access revocation.

core-alerts.observation: Default cluster/workload/storage alert rules are enabled. Those mechanisms do not establish a configured 75-percent audit capacity threshold or an SA/ISSO notification receiver.

core-keycloak.observation: Core uses identity-config 0.32.0, supports X509 and OTP by default; inactivity auto-disable is opt-in, and concurrent-session limit defaults to unlimited (0). This is platform SSO, not Horizon bundled Keycloak.

core-id-realm.observation: UDS realm defines three-failure lockout, permanentLockout=true, 600-second idle, PBKDF2-SHA256 password policy with 15 characters and classes/history/expiry; JSON event listener is enabled. Some controls remain optional.

core-id-audit.observation: UDS event listener prints user/admin events to stdout with event fields and UTC timestamps. Vector can collect these without a separately configured app forwarding agent.

core-id-notify.observation: Optional detailed-observability alerts detect user/realm/admin changes via Loki-derived metrics; enablement and receivers must be configured.

app-namespace.observation: All declared workload charts target horizon-uds; package supplies dedicated namespace, distinct workload charts and generated deployment credentials.

app-pods.observation: Candidate service chart applies non-root/read-only/no-escalation contexts, Secret references, probes and resource settings. Rendered app pods corroborate those settings; some init containers lack explicit resources.

app-web.observation: nginx serves a static SPA at /usr/share/nginx/html on port 3000, with try_files fallback, stdout/stderr logs and no configured proxy_pass, CGI or WebDAV locations.

app-web-image.observation: Multistage image copies only built Vue assets into the nginx runtime; source maps are removed. No application/OS user-management endpoint is implemented by the static nginx layer.

app-validation.observation: Global interceptor validates declared params/query/headers/JSON with Zod, enforces Content-Type, and fails routes missing a documented exemption/schema; binary/multipart paths are handled separately.

app-error.observation: Unknown/DB errors map to generic 500 problem details; HTTP transport and internal NATS dispatcher use the same mapper. Explicit application exceptions retain their supplied detail.

app-enforcer.observation: Permission enforcement resolves user/target and fails closed on missing authorization or unexpected resolution errors. Individual route metadata remains part of coverage.

app-db-role.observation: horizon_app is a distinct LOGIN role granted application DML and schema usage, not superuser/DDL by this migration; migrations/admin credentials are separate.

app-db-values.observation: DB runs under UID70 with non-root/read-only/no-escalation and dedicated PGDATA PVC; default replica count is one. Only pgaudit preload is configured, not event classes.

app-db-identity.observation: Separate admin, horizon_app and openfga_app credentials exist. Bundled Keycloak is configured to connect using the admin DB role, a least-privilege candidate gap.

app-db-extensions.observation: Migration installs pgvector/PostGIS and attempts pgaudit, catching pgaudit failures as warnings; installation and effective audit classes must not be assumed from preload.

app-permission-audit.observation: Database functions record permission changes with actor/context fields; domain audit records exist but do not cover all DBMS native logon/DDL/failed operation audit requirements.

app-auth-service.observation: Browser uses OIDC authorization-code flow, PKCE, automatic silent renew and localStorage user state. Local storage is not evidence of missing explicit logout, but idle semantics depend on the IdP.

app-logged-out.observation: Dedicated logged-out view displays an explicit logout message and return-to-login action.

app-model-profile.observation: Candidate default permits intra-namespace traffic and broad external HTTPS for chat/ingestion. MPN local inference needs a narrowed, selected model profile; model runtime is not selected here.

pg-logging.observation: PostgreSQL18 defaults connection logging disabled and disconnection logging off; failed authentication is always logged. stderr is the default server-log destination.

pgaudit-default.observation: pgAudit18 session audit classes default to none. Preload/CREATE EXTENSION alone does not enable READ/WRITE/ROLE/DDL auditing; log prefix supplies contextual identity fields.

pg-roles.observation: PostgreSQL role attributes govern LOGIN, privilege grants and connection limits; default per-role connection limit is unlimited. Superuser bypasses permission checks.

pg-password.observation: PostgreSQL18 defaults password_encryption to SCRAM-SHA-256. Existing persistent data/configuration can override defaults; generated new credentials and selected image must be distinguished from existing volumes.

pg-encryption.observation: PostgreSQL supports password hashing and transport protection; volume/block encryption requires storage-layer configuration and is not established by creating a PVC.

core-flavors.observation: Core distinguishes unicorn (curated FIPS-validated images), registry1 (Iron Bank hardening) and upstream (development/community images). The production hardened offering exists; actual selected flavor/digests and module mapping remain explicit deployment inputs.

app-jwt.observation: API uses jose jwtVerify with fixed issuer/audience/JWKS and expiry validation. It performs no online token introspection or logout/session revocation lookup; expected JWT failures are logged at debug level.

app-permission-table.observation: Append-only role-grant/revocation table includes actor user, subject user, tenant, role, action and timestamp; it does not record every request or failed authorization.

core-hardened-mesh.observation: Unicorn flavor selects curated istio-pilot-fips and istio-proxy-fips images; ambient ztunnel has its own FIPS image override. This proves the offered implementation, not the flavor of a deployed MPN cluster.

core-strict-keycloak.observation: Core Keycloak starts with --features=fips and --fips-mode=strict; cgr image handling adds the FIPS JCE security setup. Bundled Horizon Keycloak is a different chart and must not inherit these flags by name alone.

core-provision.observation: Production requires externally supplied gateway TLS chains, Loki/Velero object stores and a Keycloak database/user. Core cannot determine the supplied CA approvals, storage encryption or bucket lifecycle by itself.

core-tests.observation: Core supplies automated validation/integration tasks; the source demonstrates available checks but cannot demonstrate an MPN operator ran or scheduled them.

core-notify-default.observation: detailedObservability.alerts.enabled=false by default; user/admin modification alert templates are not enabled simply by deploying the default Core chart.

core-consent.observation: UDS theme implements the USG notice and an explicit acceptance action, but realm TERMS_AND_CONDITIONS required action is disabled by default. Enablement must be configured for the actual entry path.

kc-cookie-provider.observation: Keycloak26.7.2 cookie builder sets realm/request path, secure flag from the effective request context and HttpOnly/SameSite from CookieScope. It does not set a cross-host Domain attribute.

kc-cookie-types.observation: AUTH_SESSION_ID and KEYCLOAK_IDENTITY use FEDERATION (HttpOnly) scope; KEYCLOAK_SESSION intentionally uses FEDERATION_JS scope and is JavaScript-readable for session status.

kc-cookie-scope.observation: FEDERATION scope is SameSite=None/HttpOnly=true; FEDERATION_JS is SameSite=None/HttpOnly=false. Not all product cookies are authentication bearer secrets.

app-ci.observation: Build workflow defines image scanning, unit/integration/E2E gates, coverage report artifacts and digest-bound releases. Configured jobs do not prove execution for an unspecified delivered release.

app-codeql.observation: CodeQL runs for code changes and on a weekly schedule with SARIF artifacts and reviewed suppression processing.

app-updates.observation: Weekly automation resolves security advisories and opens labelled security-update PRs; a PR is not proof of delivered patch currency.

app-review-process.observation: Scanner findings/suppressions require justification, reviewer approval and linked tracking with expiry/review criteria.
